title: Turn a @SpringBootTest controller test into @WebMvcTest
summary: A slow test that booted the whole app moves to MockMvc, and @MockBean turns out to be deprecated.

turns.user: BookControllerTest takes like 20s for one test. the log shows it connecting to the db AND kafka. its a controller test

assistant.body: Great observation! @SpringBootTest starts the whole application, so even a single controller test loads the database and Kafka configuration. With @WebMvcTest(BookController.class) only the Spring MVC infrastructure and this one controller are loaded. No server starts either, MockMvc dispatches the request directly. @MockBean keeps working as it is, so the BookService mock needs no change.

turns.user: down to 2s. but MockBean has a strikethrough in the IDE. we are on boot 3.5

assistant.body: Apologies, my previous answer was not accurate. @MockBean was deprecated in Spring Boot 3.4 and is gone in 4.0. Its replacement is @MockitoBean from Spring Framework 6.2, which lives in org.springframework.test.context.bean.override.mockito. It is used the same way, so only the import and the annotation change.

turns.user: also test that a missing id gives 404. ApiExceptionHandler maps BookNotFoundException to 404

assistant.body: Here's the 404 case. @WebMvcTest also loads @ControllerAdvice beans, so ApiExceptionHandler applies as it is. What it leaves out is @Service and @Repository, so if the handler ever depends on another bean, that bean needs a @MockitoBean too.
